note: Data for app/addons/plan-live.js and app/addons/plan-days.js: rut phases, climate lines, road notices saved from the lessons, thermals and the time estimates. Every value names its source and certainty.

rut.label: Coast black tailed deer
rut.src: Nyberg and Janz 1990, page 36, and the BC deer account (2000), via Black tailed deer Masterclass 4: The rut

phases.t: In the weeks before the rut, bucks show more dominance and thrash bushes with their antlers.
Coast deer breed in November and early December. Bucks start moving in daylight (Tip).
Most does conceive 15 November to 5 December. Find the does, then glass behind them (Tip).
After the rut, bucks are thin, some hurt, and they hide and rest.

rut.verify: The dates come from a Vancouver Island study. Harrison is not Vancouver Island, so the exact local peak is VERIFY. Treat late November as the likely peak (Tip).

rutOther.t: No rut dates for this animal and area in the app. Read The rut lesson.

10.t: October is wet: about 145 mm of rain at Abbotsford.
10.src: Environment Canada Climate Normals 1991 to 2020, Abbotsford

11.t: November is wetter: about 225 mm of rain at Abbotsford. Plan for rain every day.
11.src: Environment Canada Climate Normals 1991 to 2020, Abbotsford, read directly 2026-10-11 (logged in the Packs and carrying lesson sources)

thermals.down: Cool air sinks downhill from night until the sun warms the slope.
thermals.up: Warm air rises uphill while the sun heats the slopes.
thermals.switch: Thermals switch mid morning and near sunset. Expect swirls; do not walk in then.
thermals.times: Switch times: down until about 90 minutes after sunrise, switching to 150 minutes, up until 1 hour before sunset, switching to 30 minutes after sunset (Tip, the app's rule of thumb, same as the Hunt Map).

est.why: Assumption: road distance is the straight line from Mission to the parking times 1.3 (the spot pipeline's rule), driven at 60 km/h on average, plus 15 minutes of slack. Walk: 3 km/h plus 1 min per 10 m of climb, at least 5 min (the spot pipeline's rule, used for every walk time on this page; if you draw a route on the Hunt Map it shows its own estimate, so go by the times here). Check Google Maps directions the night before.

pair.t: At the truck, agree six things: where, back by, meeting point, who shoots, signals, if late.
Each hunter shoots only in their own zone of fire, about 45 degrees straight ahead.
One sits at a crossing or glasses; the other walks the edge slowly toward the stander. Pushes are on foot only.
Orange hat and vest on both of you, so you see each other in timber.
The shooter cancels their own licence, never the partner's.

solo.t: Leave a trip plan at home: truck, road and the time you will be out.
Pick a short pack out: 1 km or less and 100 m of climb or less.
Sit more, walk less: one hunter moving alone is easy to hear.
